dish_drainer_compound_2_top_hung.notes: THE HEADING IS MISSING THE WORD 'COMPOUND' AND THE POSITION IS ONE ANYWAY. printed p.225 heads this 'Dish-drainer unit with top-hung door' while the identical position at H.36 and H.48 is headed 'Compound dish-drainer unit with top-hung door' - and this one carries module splits and the compound rule all the same. The description above is the page's own wording (rule: the registry keeps the catalog's), the type key says what it is. Suffix 06 matches both other families. Carries the printed rule: 'In compound wall units, the dish-drainer rack is fitted in the widest unit.' Also gains '1 shelf', which the H.36 and H.48 twins do not print.

dish_drainer_compound_2_push_up.notes: SUFFIX 14, AND THE THIRD DIFFERENT ANSWER FOR THE SAME IDEA. A compound push-up dish-drainer is 11 at H.48 (PC1811, one code, 180 wide, 90+90) and 14 here (two codes, 90 in 45+45 and 120 in 60+60); H.36 has no such position at all. Three families, three shapes. It does match this family's own plain compound push-up widths (PD0908 / PD1208) exactly - so within a family the two compounds agree, and across families nothing does. Carries the printed rule: 'In compound wall units, the dish-drainer rack is fitted in the widest unit.'

front_layout.note: One push-up door across both modules. NO hinge_axis.
